subject: Post-demo: Prompt set & model recommendations for BrightRetail
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Chris Park <chris.park@brightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Prompt set & model recommendations for BrightRetail

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for taking the demo with us today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goal: Improve customer support summarization and response suggestion for your returns team (short, 2–3 sentence replies).
- Key constraints you mentioned: 1) strict PII redaction for customer IDs and payment info, 2) 300–500 token output cap per response, 3) sub-100ms SLO for first-token latency on common queries.

To help us run a focused model-fit evaluation, could you send: 
1) A representative set of 50–100 real prompts (anonymized/redacted) covering happy-path, edge cases, and denial/appeal scenarios.
2) A couple of examples of the current expected reply for 10 of those prompts (for quality baseline).

I'm attaching a small prompt collection template to make it easier to share (CSV). If you prefer, drop a doc in the Drive link below.

On our side, initial recommendations based on what we saw today: 
- Recommended models: rw-instruct-13B-ptq (cost-effective) and rw-flan-34B-q4 (higher-quality fallback).
- Eval plan: run both models on the provided prompt set + your 10 baselines, measure ROUGE/EM/semantic-sim, and surface latency/cost tradeoffs.

Next steps: if you can send the prompt set this week, Marissa and I will kick off the eval and share a short benchmark report by EOW next week.

Thanks —
Logan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prompt_set_template.csv (text/csv)]
[Drive: https://redwood-drive.internal/benchmarks/2026-07-latency-quality-brightretail]

From: Chris Park <chris.park@brightretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Prompt set & model recommendations for BrightRetail

Thanks Logan — forwarding the sample prompts we used in the demo. I redacted customer names and payment tokens per our policy. A couple notes: 

- Attached is a short doc with 60 prompts across returns, exchanges, and warranty questions. Some of the edge cases include multi-turn context where the agent needs to reference a prior message.
- Question: what's your recommended approach for PII redaction? We currently remove card numbers but keep a unique customer_id. Do you want the customer_id replaced with a stable token (e.g., <CUST_ID_123>) in the prompt set?

Attaching: brightretail_sample_prompts.docx

Chris
Head of Product Operations
BrightRetail
[Attachment: brightretail_sample_prompts.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Chris Park <chris.park@brightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Prompt set & model recommendations for BrightRetail

Appreciate that, Chris — this is perfect. A few quick answers and clarifications: 

PII/redaction guidance: 
- Best practice for our evals is to normalize any persistent identifiers to stable tokens (e.g., <CUST_ID_1>, <ORDER_12345>) so the models don't memorize raw identifiers. Remove full card numbers and any stripe/payment tokens.
- For multi-turn context, include the last 2 user turns in the prompt examples and mark system instructions if applicable.

Prompt set template: please copy the attached CSV into one row per prompt with columns: prompt_id, category, conversation_history, user_prompt, expected_reply (if available), tags (edge_case/denial/etc.). I've attached the template again.

Model recommendations and benchmark links: 
- Start with rw-instruct-13B-ptq for cost/baseline. If quality gaps appear on denial/appeal wording, run rw-flan-34B-q4 as a higher-quality candidate.
- Internal benchmark we use for similar support workloads: https://redwood-drive.internal/benchmarks/2026-07-latency-quality-brightretail (contains latency/cost per 1k tokens and sample eval metrics).

Marissa — looping you in to coordinate the eval run and to collect the completed CSV. Marissa, can you confirm we have capacity on the Dedicated test pool for early next week?

Thanks —
Logan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prompt_set_template.csv (text/csv)]

From: Chris Park <chris.park@brightretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Reilly <liam@brightretail.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Prompt set & model recommendations for BrightRetail

Thanks, Logan and Marissa —

We'll standardize the IDs to tokens and fill out the CSV by Monday. Two quick asks while you run the eval: 
1) Can you surface any known quality regressions when moving from the 13B quantized model to the 34B q4? We care most about tone and legal/returns wording staying accurate.
2) If you see hallucination risks on appeal denials, what's the recommended mitigation (tune system prompt, add conservative post-filter)?

If you can include a short section in the benchmark report answering those two points that'd be very helpful for our legal and ops teams.

Appreciate it —
Chris
Head of Product Operations
BrightRetail
thread_summary: Follow-up after product demo; customer to provide anonymized prompt set. Redwood recommended rw-instruct-13B-ptq (baseline) and rw-flan-34B-q4 (fallback). Asked for redaction guidance and requested benchmark report to include known quality regressions and hallucination mitigations.
